    #Tutorial 1 (Fundamental Concepts)

    #Question 1

    #Part (i)

    Initial Equilibrium State

    Pgas​=Patm​+Ppiston​+Plock​

    108×103=100×103+0.0325(9.81)​+0.032Flock​​

    Flock​=206.95 N

    Final Equilibrium State

    102×103=100×103+0.0325(9.81)​+0.032Flock​​

    Flock​=14.95 N

    #Part (ii)

    As the system is not in equilibrium, the piston moves up rapidly when lock L1​ is released. Thus, there are rapid changes in the pressure and volume of the gas.
    Hence, this creates sharp gradients in the intensive properties of the gas, and
    it is not possible to assign uniform single values to the properties. The gas
    undergoes a non-quasi equilibrium process.

    When the piston reaches L2​, the properties of the gas progressively becomes
    uniform until a state of equilibrium is reached. Thus, when the system is in
    equilibrium, intensive properties can be assigned unique values.

    #Part (iii)

    Weights totaling 21.1kg, which produces the same pressure as L1​, can be placed on the piston. These weights are then removed one by one, allowing the piston to slowly move up. Thus, pressure and volume of the gas does not change rapidly. The weights are removed until 1.524kg is left, which is the pressure produced by L2​.

    #Tutorial 10 (Bernoulli Equation)

    #Question 1

    Using gage pressure at each of the points.

    P0​+21​ρV0​2+ρgz0​=P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​

    ρgh=ρgh1​

    h1​=h

    P0​+21​ρV0​2+ρgz0​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​

    ρgh=ρgh2​

    h2​=h

    Pressure at the free surface is equal to atmosphere pressure. Since it is a large tank, the velocity at the free surface is negligible. Pressure of the first two streams is also equal
    to atmospheric pressure and at the maximum height, velocity is zero.

    P0​+21​ρV0​2+ρgz0​=P3​+21​ρV3​2+ρgz3​

    ρgh=21​ρV3​2

    V3​=2gh​

    Fluid stream exits the third pipe with a velocity that is directed 45° from horizontal.
    Only the velocity’s vertical component results in an increase in height of the stream.

    P3​+21​ρV3​2+ρgz3​=P3′​+21​ρV3′​2+ρgz3′​

    21​ρ(2gh​⋅cos45°)2=ρgh3​

    21​ρgh=ρgh3​

    h3​=21​h

    Pressure at the exit of the pipe and apex of the stream are both equal to atmospheric pressure. Vertical component of velocity at the apex of the stream is equal to zero.

    #Question 2

    Taking the interface as the datum for height and using gage pressure.

    P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​

    700(9.81)(4)=1000(9.81)h

    h=2.8 m

    P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​=Pnozzle​+21​ρVnozzle​2+ρgznozzle​

    1000(9.81)(2.8)=21​(1000)Vnozzle​2

    Vnozzle​=7.4119 m/s

    Using continuity equation,

    Apipe​Vpipe​=Anozzle​Vnozzle​

    π(0.1)2Vpipe​=π(0.05)2(7.4119)

    Vpipe​=1.8530 m/s

    P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​=Ppipe​+21​ρVpipe​2+ρgzpipe​

    700(9.81)(4)=Ppipe​+21​(1000)(1.8530)2−1000(9.81)(1)

    Ppipe​=35.561 kPa

    #Tutorial 11 (Continuity Equation)

    #Question 1

    Assume a steady flow, incompressible fluid, and a uniform exit velocity.
    Taking the control volume as the enclosing region around the disk.

    dtdmsys​​=∂t∂​∫CV​ ρ dV+∫CS​ ρ(V⋅n) dA

    0=∫CS​ ρ(V⋅n) dA

    0=ρ(∫inlet​ V⋅n dA+∫exit​ V⋅n dA)

    0=ρ(−Vi​Ai​+∫exit​ Ve​cos60° dA)

    ρVi​Ai​=ρ(Ve​cos60°)Ae​

    m˙i​=1000(3cos60°)⋅2π(0.18)(0.03)

    m˙i​=50.894 kg/s

    #Question 2

    dtdmsys​​=∂t∂​∫CV​ ρ dV+∫CS​ ρ(V⋅n) dA

    0=∫inlet​ ρVi​cos180° dA+∫exit​ ρVe​cos0° dA

    0=−∫inlet​ ρV dA+∫exit​ ρu dA

    0=−ρV(0.2×1)+∫exit​ ρ(4y−2y2)(1⋅dy)

    0.2V=∫00.3​ 4y−2y2 dy

    0.2V=[2y2−32​y3]00.3​

    V=0.81 m/s

    #Question 3

    Let the control volume be the tank.

    Mass of air inside is not constant, the second term in the equation is not zero.

    However, the mass of air in the system remains a constant and thus, dtdmsys​​ is zero.

    dtdmsys​​=∂t∂​∫CV​ ρ dV+∫CS​ ρ(V⋅n) dA

    0=∂t∂​ mCV​+∫inlet​ ρi​Vi​cos180° dA+∫exit​ ρe​Ve​ dA

    0=∂t∂​ mCV​−∫inlet​ ρi​Vi​ dA+∫exit​ ρe​Ve​ dA

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=∫inlet​ ρi​Vi​ dA−∫exit​ ρe​Ve​ dA

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=ρi​Vi​Ai​−ρe​Ve​Ae​

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=ρi​Qi​−ρe​Ve​Ae​

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=1.2(0.3)−1.8(210)π(0.015)2

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=0.092808 kg/s

    Assuming density in the tank is uniformly distributed, ρ is a constant.

    ∂t∂​ mCV​=∂t∂​ ρV

    ∂t∂ρ​=0.60.092808​

    ∂t∂ρ​=0.15468 kg/m3

    Since ∂t∂​ mCV​ is positive, the mass of air in the tank is increasing.

    Since ∂t∂ρ​ is positive, the density of air in the tank is also increasing.
